# Career Education Institute course specs

Generated 2026-10-20 by `npm run course-specs`. Do not edit by hand: change `src/data/course-pricing.mjs` (hours) or the career data, then run the script again.

Each job-title training is self-paced online with 12 months of LMS access, ends with a final knowledge check and awards a certificate of completion. Seat time below is the target the website advertises, so build each course to that length.

## Price ladder

| Length | Price per learner |
|---|---|
| 6 hours | $59.99 |
| 8 hours | $74.99 |
| 10 hours | $89.99 |
| 12 hours | $109.99 |
| 14 hours | $129.99 |

Volume discounts at checkout and on quotes: 2 to 10 seats 1%, 11 to 20 seats 2%, 21 to 50 seats 3%, 51 to 100 seats 5%, 101 to 250 seats 7%, 251 to 500 seats 8%, 501 to 1000 seats 10%.

## Module plans

### Acupuncturist Training: 12 hours, $109.99

| # | Module | Time | Lessons |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Introduction to the Acupuncturist Role | 1 hr | What acupuncturists do and why the role matters; Where they work: settings, employers and teams; Pay, job outlook and the career ladder; Professional and ethical expectations |
| 2 | A Day on the Job | 45 min | A realistic shift, start to finish; Schedules, shifts and workload; Working with supervisors, coworkers and customers; The best and hardest parts of the job |
| 3 | Essential Acupuncturist Vocabulary | 1 hr 10 min | Key term: Acupoint; Key term: Meridian; Key term: Qi; Key term: Cupping; Key term: Moxibustion; Plus 10 more terms with practice drills |
| 4 | Core Duties and Responsibilities | 1 hr 10 min | Take health histories; Assess patients; Insert acupuncture needles; Use cupping and heat therapies; Advise on lifestyle |
| 5 | Common Tasks, Step by Step | 2 hr 40 min | How to practice clean needle technique; How to do a first visit intake; How to market a new practice; Common mistakes and how to avoid them |
| 6 | Tools, Equipment and Technology | 1 hr | Sterile acupuncture needles; Treatment tables; Cupping sets; Heat lamps; Sharps containers |
| 7 | Safety, Compliance and Professional Standards | 1 hr 25 min | Use sterile single-use needles; Screen for contraindications; Dispose of sharps safely; Watch for fainting during treatment |
| 8 | Skills Employers Look For | 1 hr | Point location; Needling technique; Patient assessment; Calm presence; Listening |
| 9 | Launching Your Acupuncturist Career | 1 hr | Education and training pathways; Credential overview: NCCAOM certification; Credential overview: State acupuncture license; Resume and interview preparation; Your first 90 days on the job |
| 10 | Final Knowledge Check | 1 hr | Comprehensive practice exam with explanations; Certificate of completion on passing |

### Anesthesiologist Training: 12 hours, $109.99

| # | Module | Time | Lessons |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Introduction to the Anesthesiologist Role | 1 hr | What anesthesiologists do and why the role matters; Where they work: settings, employers and teams; Pay, job outlook and the career ladder; Professional and ethical expectations |
| 2 | A Day on the Job | 45 min | A realistic shift, start to finish; Schedules, shifts and workload; Working with supervisors, coworkers and customers; The best and hardest parts of the job |
| 3 | Essential Anesthesiologist Vocabulary | 1 hr 10 min | Key term: Induction; Key term: Intubation; Key term: MAC; Key term: Spinal anesthesia; Key term: Epidural; Plus 10 more terms with practice drills |
| 4 | Core Duties and Responsibilities | 1 hr 10 min | Evaluate patients before anesthesia; Plan and give anesthesia; Manage airways and breathing; Monitor vital signs during surgery; Manage pain after surgery |
| 5 | Common Tasks, Step by Step | 2 hr 40 min | How to conduct a preoperative evaluation; How to run an operating room crisis; How to place an ultrasound-guided nerve block; Common mistakes and how to avoid them |
| 6 | Tools, Equipment and Technology | 1 hr | Anesthesia machines; Patient monitors; Video laryngoscopes; Ultrasound; Infusion pumps |
| 7 | Safety, Compliance and Professional Standards | 1 hr 25 min | Complete machine and drug checks; Use time-outs before procedures; Prevent medication errors with labeling; Follow infection control |
| 8 | Skills Employers Look For | 1 hr | Anesthesia pharmacology; Airway management; Critical care; Calm under pressure; Vigilance |
| 9 | Launching Your Anesthesiologist Career | 1 hr | Education and training pathways; Credential overview: Board certification (ABA); Credential overview: State medical license; Resume and interview preparation; Your first 90 days on the job |
| 10 | Final Knowledge Check | 1 hr | Comprehensive practice exam with explanations; Certificate of completion on passing |

### Audiologist Training: 12 hours, $109.99

| # | Module | Time | Lessons |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Introduction to the Audiologist Role | 1 hr | What audiologists do and why the role matters; Where they work: settings, employers and teams; Pay, job outlook and the career ladder; Professional and ethical expectations |
| 2 | A Day on the Job | 45 min | A realistic shift, start to finish; Schedules, shifts and workload; Working with supervisors, coworkers and customers; The best and hardest parts of the job |
| 3 | Essential Audiologist Vocabulary | 1 hr 10 min | Key term: AuD; Key term: Audiogram; Key term: Decibel; Key term: Conductive hearing loss; Key term: Sensorineural hearing loss; Plus 10 more terms with practice drills |
| 4 | Core Duties and Responsibilities | 1 hr 10 min | Test hearing and balance; Diagnose hearing loss; Fit and program hearing aids; Manage cochlear implants; Treat tinnitus |
| 5 | Common Tasks, Step by Step | 2 hr 40 min | How to perform a pure-tone hearing test; How to fit a hearing aid; How to counsel a patient on tinnitus; Common mistakes and how to avoid them |
| 6 | Tools, Equipment and Technology | 1 hr | Audiometers; Sound booths; Tympanometers; Hearing aid software; Otoacoustic emission equipment |
| 7 | Safety, Compliance and Professional Standards | 1 hr 25 min | Clean equipment between patients; Use safe sound levels in testing; Refer sudden hearing loss urgently; Follow infection control |
| 8 | Skills Employers Look For | 1 hr | Audiometric testing; Hearing aid fitting; Cochlear implant programming; Patience; Communication |
| 9 | Launching Your Audiologist Career | 1 hr | Education and training pathways; Credential overview: State audiology license; Credential overview: CCC-A (ASHA); Resume and interview preparation; Your first 90 days on the job |
| 10 | Final Knowledge Check | 1 hr | Comprehensive practice exam with explanations; Certificate of completion on passing |

### Cardiologist Training: 12 hours, $109.99

| # | Module | Time | Lessons |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Introduction to the Cardiologist Role | 1 hr | What cardiologists do and why the role matters; Where they work: settings, employers and teams; Pay, job outlook and the career ladder; Professional and ethical expectations |
| 2 | A Day on the Job | 45 min | A realistic shift, start to finish; Schedules, shifts and workload; Working with supervisors, coworkers and customers; The best and hardest parts of the job |
| 3 | Essential Cardiologist Vocabulary | 1 hr 10 min | Key term: EKG; Key term: Echocardiogram; Key term: Myocardial infarction; Key term: Heart failure; Key term: Arrhythmia; Plus 10 more terms with practice drills |
| 4 | Core Duties and Responsibilities | 1 hr 10 min | Evaluate heart symptoms; Read EKGs and imaging; Manage heart failure and hypertension; Treat arrhythmias; Perform catheterizations and stents |
| 5 | Common Tasks, Step by Step | 2 hr 40 min | How to read a 12-lead EKG; How to respond to a STEMI alert; How to counsel a patient on heart failure; Common mistakes and how to avoid them |
